note: Calibration anchor (herb: weak). Correct motion, no surprise, text labels fail the gate.
Drapes and folds under the hand at once; yanking a clip free and the next scarf dropping in is the surprise. Faceting at folds, lift on grab too high.
Crack lands under the finger instantly, falling shards reveal the next cover. Crack lines too faint at tile size, fallen shards go grey.
Reads as ferrofluid, but spikes are shallow dimples (golf ball), pool is a uniform disc, ground washed grey. Heavy on software GL.
Light bars through open slats are lovely; the swap reads as a wipe. Close to Split Flap.
Relief exists but is muddy grey at tile size; needs harder light and bigger depth.
Looks like the print with scratches, not sand; furrows too thin to read.
Mutation A (craft): green float-glass edges on every break make the crack read at tile size; shards keep their colour as they fall.
Mutation B (A + second blow bursts at the camera): shards grow past you and fill the frame. The most striking moment of the run. Kept.
Parent re-run on the round 2 script (adds a hover pass), for a fair comparison.
Mutation A (craft): finer grid, light pool behind, lower lift. Smoother, but slower.
Mutation B (A + air): passing the pointer near it billows the silk without touching. It now answers before you click. Kept.
Parent re-run on the round 2 script.
Mutation A (craft): curved-slat shading. Marginal.
Mutation B (peek): press and two fingers part the slats in a lens, sun and the next record glowing through. A human gesture nobody has made a component of. Kept.
Wildcard mutation: sharper lattice, irregular puddle, dark ground. Still reads as a dimpled blob, and fails the pacing gate on software GL. Dropped.
Polish: burst variant made the default.
Polish: air variant default, shorter dead time before the next scarf drops in.
Polish: the gap glow no longer blows out, so the next record reads clearly through the slats; only nearby slats bend (pacing 83 to 50ms p95).
